mappings.note: The whole point is that losing a black card leaves n(S) = 51 with the queen of hearts still present, i.e. constructing the right sample space (C-8.1-LO-4). LO-3 then covers the routine 1/51.
Forms P(red) and P(blue) as simple-event ratios in an unknown x (LO-3) and solves for the favourable count (C-8.1-LO-4). No complement or compound structure.
Pair of dice, sum 8, five ordered pairs out of 36. Compound dice event, LO-4.
One ticket from 35 with 10 prizes. Simple event, LO-3.
Two coins, 'at least one head' over the four-outcome space. Compound coin event, LO-4.
Doublets on a pair of dice, 6 of 36. Compound dice event, LO-4.
One die, prime face. Simple event, LO-3.
x^2 < 4 over seven listed integers. Single draw, LO-3.
Perfect squares among 1 to 80. Simple event, LO-3.
'Not red' states the event as the complement of the red balls. Complement outcome, LO-4.
'Not divisible by 3' is computed as 30 - 10, an explicit complement of the multiples of 3. LO-4, not LO-3.
Multiples of 5 among cards 11 to 30, with n(S) = 20 rather than 30. Simple event, LO-3.
Two sub-parts both over the 36-pair space: each die even, and sum 5. Compound dice events throughout, LO-4.
Vowel and consonant counted directly out of 26. Although the two parts happen to be complementary, each is a positively stated simple event, so LO-3 rather than LO-4.
Two coins: at least one head, and exactly one head with one tail. Both are compound coin events over {HH, HT, TH, TT}, LO-4.
Both parts are negations - 'not a white ball' and 'neither green nor red'. The complement outcome, LO-4.
'Not red' over three colours. Complement outcome, LO-4.

A two-child family is a two-stage experiment whose four-outcome space {GG, GB, BG, BB} has to be written out, so C-8.1-LO-4 leads; LO-4 carries the compound structure, whose wording names only cards, dice and coins.
The difficulty is that the sample space is the seven possible pairs of leftover days, not 366: C-8.1-LO-4. LO-3 covers the resulting 2/7.
Two coins, both heads or both tails. Compound coin event, LO-4.
Part (i) 'non face card' is the complement of the 12 face cards (LO-4); part (ii) black king is a plain simple event (LO-3). The two sub-parts genuinely sit on different outcomes.
Part (ii) is obtained as 1 - P(buy) and cross-checked against the direct count, which is exactly the complement rule (LO-4); part (i) is the simple event 'good pen' (LO-3).
Two dice, product below 18, counted die by die over 36 outcomes. Compound dice event, LO-4.
Cards 11 to 123 give n(S) = 113; perfect squares and multiples of 7 are each counted directly. Two simple events on one draw, LO-3.
Sets up P before and after adding six red balls and solves the doubling condition (LO-3), the answer being a favourable count (C-8.1-LO-4). No complement or compound event.
